newsitem.title: FRANCE: Five climbers found dead in French Alps.
newsitem.headline: Five climbers found dead in French Alps.

text.p: Rescuers on Tuesday found the bodies of five climbers who fell to their deaths in four separate accidents in the French Alps.

Rescuers said French climbers Thierry Renard, 65, and Georges Ripert, 54, were found dead after falling 300 metres (1,000 ft) while roped together at an altitude of 3,700 metres (12,000 ft) near Grenoble.
A German climber, aged 29, fell about 100 metres (330 ft) to his death while coming down from the 4,100-metre (13,500 ft) Aiguille Verte, near Mont Blanc. His name was not disclosed.
A Frenchwoman aged 50 fell to her death while climbing Mont Charvin, rescue workers said. They did not immediately release her identity.
Finally the body of a man estimated to be in his twenties was found near the summit of Les Agneaux. Rescue workers said the man may have been missing since November 1996.
More than 40 climbers and hikers have died in France this summer.
